course.title: Python Decorators: From @ Syntax to Descriptors

outcomes.text: Desugar any decorated definition, stacked or with arguments, into plain calls
outcomes.observable: Rewrite a given @-decorated function or class as explicit assignments and predict its printed output and call order

outcomes.text: Write a correct function decorator with functools.wraps that preserves metadata and handles any signature
outcomes.observable: Implement a timing or logging decorator that passes *args/**kwargs through and keeps __name__ and __doc__

outcomes.text: Write a decorator factory that takes arguments, including the optional-argument form
outcomes.observable: Implement @retry(times=3) and a decorator usable both as @dec and @dec(...)

outcomes.text: Apply common decorator patterns: registration, caching, attribute tagging and class decorators
outcomes.observable: Build a plugin registry decorator and a class decorator that adds a method, and explain when each runs

outcomes.text: Explain how @property, @classmethod and @staticmethod work via the descriptor protocol and decorate methods correctly
outcomes.observable: Predict what obj.attr returns for a given descriptor and write a reusable validator descriptor

exclusions.why: Alternative class-customisation tools, a separate topic beyond decorators
Type-checker detail not needed to write or understand working decorators

exclusions.text: Async and generator-specific decorators, contextlib.contextmanager internals
exclusions.why: Builds on coroutines and generators, which this course does not teach

exclusions.text: Framework decorators (Flask routes, pytest fixtures, dataclasses internals)
exclusions.why: Library-specific APIs; the course teaches the mechanism they all share

exclusions.text: Third-party wrapper libraries such as wrapt
exclusions.why: Optional tooling; functools covers what a working learner needs

stages.title: Python decorators: functions, factories, classes and descriptors
